interest: Shows US screening of Bata Shoe visa applicants for Axis ties, and a 1942 finding of no Japanese agents.
overview: Cross-reference sheets on Japanese and Axis activity in Haiti: an October 1940 note on Bata Shoe manager Frantisek Votava's suspicious visa request, and a January 1942 telegram confirming no Japanese propaganda or commercial agents remained in the country.

people.name: Frantisek Votava
people.role: Manager of the shoe factory of Chaussures Bata Haiti, S.A.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a despatch on Frantisek Votava, manager of Chaussures Bata Haiti, S.A., and his application for a U.S. visitor's visa amidst investigation of Axis activities.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on a 1940 despatch: the Legation viewed Bata Shoe manager Frantisek Votava with suspicion, requesting background checks.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on Bata Shoe Company and Frantisek Votava Visa Application

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a telegram reporting that no Japanese propaganda or business representatives were present in Haiti.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a January 1942 telegram: Minister White confirmed no Japanese propaganda or commercial agents were operating in Haiti.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on Japanese Propaganda and Commercial Representation in Haiti
